title: ML fairness requires balancing accuracy and protected attributes in credit decisions
claim: ML models for credit assessment must trade off predictive accuracy against fairness, addressing algorithmic bias in protected characteristics (gender, race, age)

source.epub_locator: Chapter 1: Introduction to fairness in lending

support: Chapter explicitly discusses balancing accuracy vs fairness concerns in credit models
mechanism: Fair ML constrains model predictions to reduce disparate impact; constraints may reduce overall accuracy on majority populations
assumptions: Historical data biases can be corrected
failure_modes: Insufficient fairness leads to regulatory action
validation: Regulatory compliance, fairness-accuracy curves, demographic parity testing

title: Model transparency alone does not guarantee fairness or prevent bias
claim: Explainability methods like SHAP/LIME make models interpretable but do not inherently eliminate unfairness; transparency is necessary but insufficient for bias mitigation
support: Chapter discusses how transparency can reveal unfair patterns without fixing them
mechanism: Transparency enables detection of bias but requires active fairness interventions (reweighting, constraint-based optimization) to correct it
assumptions: Interpretable models may have lower predictive power
failure_modes: Transparency reveals unfairness but remedies are insufficient
Regulatory gaming with fake fairness metrics
validation: Audit interpretability vs fairness metrics; test model behavior under fairness constraints

title: HFT infrastructure requires sub-millisecond latency and sophisticated real-time risk controls
claim: High-frequency trading viability depends on low-latency technology stack, colocation, direct market access, and automated risk management to prevent execution failures
support: Chapter details infrastructure requirements and real-time risk systems for HFT
mechanism: Lower latency enables faster reaction to market signals and reduces adverse selection; risk controls prevent cascade failures from execution errors
assumptions: Technology investments are justified by alpha
validation: Benchmark infrastructure requirements; simulate failure modes; compare with market data

title: Real-time sentiment analysis can detect market regime shifts but requires careful validation
claim: Sentiment analysis on news/social media detects short-term market sentiment and may signal regime shifts; predictive power requires rigorous out-of-sample validation

source.epub_locator: Case studies on sentiment impacting trading

support: Chapter includes case studies on sentiment analysis for HFT
mechanism: Market participants react to news; sentiment signals capture early reaction before price adjustment; overcrowding reduces alpha
assumptions: Sentiment data is timely and accurate
Market impact is not too large
validation: Out-of-sample testing, walk-forward analysis, sensitivity to data source and sentiment provider

title: Reinforcement learning agents (PPO) can learn trading policies but require careful design and validation
claim: Proximal Policy Optimization and similar RL methods can learn trading strategies; success depends on reward design, environment realism, and preventing overfitting to historical data

source.epub_locator: Chapter 5: RL trading agents and performance

support: Chapter discusses PPO-based robo-traders and empirical results
mechanism: RL agents optimize for reward signal; realistic environment and carefully shaped rewards improve transferability to live trading
assumptions: Reward is well-specified for trading objective
validation: Out-of-sample testing, policy robustness checks, stress testing with historical crises

title: Algorithmic trading best practices include systematic risk management and constant monitoring
claim: Leading algorithmic trading implementations emphasize rigorous backtesting, risk limits, real-time monitoring, and rapid intervention protocols to prevent loss cascades

source.epub_locator: Chapter 6: Best practices and case studies

support: Chapter surveys algorithmic trading implementations and identifies common practices
mechanism: Position limits cap exposure; stop-loss orders minimize losses; monitoring detects anomalies; intervention procedures halt trading if needed
assumptions: Market conditions remain within historical ranges
failure_modes: Model risk - risk models fail in extreme conditions
validation: Regulatory compliance, stress testing, post-trade analysis

title: Anomaly detection systems improve HFT risk management and reduce execution failures
claim: Real-time anomaly detection identifies unusual market conditions and execution errors before they cause significant losses; combined with automated circuit breakers
support: Chapter discusses anomaly detection methods for real-time risk in HFT
mechanism: Statistical models detect outliers in price, volume, spread, execution metrics; circuit breakers halt trading on triggers
validation: Compare anomaly signals vs. realized risk; measure false positive/negative rates; stress test with historical crises

title: LSTM and time-series models capture temporal dependencies for price prediction
claim: LSTM networks and similar sequential models learn temporal patterns in cryptocurrency prices; backtesting shows improved forecasting accuracy vs. baseline

source.epub_locator: Chapter 13: ML for crypto price prediction

support: Chapter applies LSTM to cryptocurrency price forecasting with empirical results
mechanism: LSTM learns long-term dependencies via cell state; sequential structure naturally models price momentum and mean reversion
failure_modes: Transaction costs not captured in backtest
validation: Cross-validation, walk-forward analysis, out-of-sample testing on held-out dates

title: Portfolio optimization with ML-predicted returns requires careful risk calibration
claim: Using ML price predictions to optimize portfolio weights improves Sharpe ratio in backtests; live performance depends on prediction alpha remaining after transaction costs and slippage
support: Chapter combines ML forecasts with Markowitz portfolio optimization
mechanism: ML predictions improve return forecasts; optimization allocates capital to highest risk-adjusted opportunities; diversification reduces volatility
validation: Out-of-sample Sharpe ratio, portfolio turnover analysis, sensitivity to transaction costs

title: LSTM and XGBoost classifiers achieve high accuracy in high-frequency futures market prediction
claim: Optimized LSTM and XGBoost models trained on high-frequency futures data achieve 60-70% classification accuracy for directional predictions
support: Chapter reports detailed performance metrics on HF futures classification tasks
mechanism: LSTM captures temporal patterns; XGBoost captures non-linear feature interactions; both outperform linear models on financial data
failure_modes: Profitable signals obscured by transaction costs
validation: Out-of-sample testing, walk-forward analysis, comparison with random baseline, sensitivity to hyperparameters

title: Volatility transmission between markets indicates interdependence and regime coupling
claim: Dynamic volatility models reveal significant spillover effects between domestic equity and global markets; volatility shocks propagate with measurable delays and magnitudes
support: Chapter applies GARCH/DCC models to analyze volatility spillovers between markets
mechanism: Information arrival and market-wide shock propagation causes volatility clustering; time-zone staggering delays transmission; correlation structures depend on asset class
failure_modes: Market structure changes (new trading venues) alter dynamics
Non-linear spillovers not captured by linear models
validation: Out-of-sample volatility prediction, cross-market stress tests

title: NLP sentiment analysis extracts market-relevant signals from news and social media
claim: Natural language processing on financial news, earnings calls, and social media sentiment correlates with short-term price movements; sentiment-based signals show predictive power
support: Chapter surveys NLP applications including sentiment analysis, entity extraction, and topic modeling for trading signals
mechanism: Market participants respond to news; sentiment captures early reaction; NLP scales sentiment extraction to high-volume data sources
assumptions: Sentiment is tradeable within execution timeframe
validation: Out-of-sample sentiment alpha, turnover analysis, comparison with published indices (VIX, Fear/Greed)

title: Advanced NLP models (BERT, Transformers) improve financial text understanding but require domain adaptation
claim: Pre-trained transformer models (BERT, GPT) transfer well to finance tasks; fine-tuning on financial data improves accuracy; context-awareness captures nuance in financial language
support: Chapter discusses transformer architecture and transfer learning for financial NLP
mechanism: Transformers learn contextual word representations; self-attention captures long-range dependencies; fine-tuning adapts to financial domain
failure_modes: Domain shift reduces transfer learning benefit
validation: Task-specific evaluation (sentiment classification, entity extraction); compare with domain-specific vs. general models

title: Multiple ML forecasting methods improve predictions when combined via ensemble methods
claim: Combining ARIMA, LSTM, XGBoost, and other forecasters via voting or weighted averaging outperforms individual models on out-of-sample financial data
support: Chapter applies multiple forecasting methods to financial time-series and demonstrates ensemble benefits
mechanism: Ensemble reduces model-specific bias and variance; different methods capture different market regimes; averaging smooths prediction errors
failure_modes: All methods fail simultaneously in regime shift
Correlation of models reduces ensemble benefit
Equal weighting suboptimal vs. adaptive weighting
validation: Out-of-sample forecasting accuracy, sensitivity to model weights, comparison with simple average

title: Backtesting results often overstate live trading performance due to data quality, look-ahead bias, and cost assumptions
claim: Published backtesting results commonly achieve inflated Sharpe ratios due to look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, optimistic cost assumptions, and insufficient walk-forward validation
support: Chapter discusses backtesting pitfalls and the gap between simulation and live performance
mechanism: Look-ahead bias: using future information to train models; Survivorship bias: only successful strategies published; Cost bias: underestimating spreads, slippage, commissions; Overfitting: optimizing parameters on historical data
assumptions: Live market conditions differ from backtest assumptions
failure_modes: Strategy fails in live trading despite high backtest returns
Significant gap between backtest and live Sharpe
Parameter sensitivity not captured in backtest
